attributes.scope: MWCC GC 1.2.5 family; boundary refinement of claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast - narrows when its declared-alias counter-form should be preferred vs a repeated inline cast, specifically for multi-site field WRITES off a plain (non-walked, non-indexed) pointer.

subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: claim.law.declared-alias-vs-repeated-cast's counter-form (declare ONE typed alias, use it at every site) does NOT transfer to a plain (non-walked, non-indexed) struct-member pointer whose fields are being WRITTEN with already-computed values, when the raw-offset source expresses each site as an INDEPENDENT `*(T*)((u8*)ptr + N)` dereference with no shared variable (as opposed to the parent law's evidence, where the pre-existing fakematch source already used REPEATED NAMED-TYPE casts). Verified twice in game/anim/atree.c on already-100%-matched functions: (1) AtreeNodeInit's 3 sequential writes `*(f32*)((u8*)node->obj+0x30)=node->x; ...+0x34...=node->y; ...+0x38...=node->z;` regressed real 0->6 (target-only +2 lwz) when converted to `MBObject* nodeObj=(MBObject*)node->obj; nodeObj->mat[3][0]=node->x; ...` - reverting to a fresh `((MBObject*)node->obj)->mat[3][0]=node->x;` cast at each of the 3 sites restored real 0. (2) AnimFixPos (inlined into DoAnimateTree)'s 2 mat[3][0]/[2] writes off child->obj plus 4 animdata.ppos/xpos writes off child->anim (6 sites total, all storing the same constant sAtreeZero) regressed real 0->39 (target-only +5 lwz) with a declared `MBObject*`/`animdata*` alias per pointer, and again returned to real 0 with a fresh inline cast at every site. In both cases the declared alias let MWCC cache the loaded pointer value in a register across all field writes, eliminating reload instructions the TARGET binary actually contains - meaning the target's own original C source must have re-expressed the pointer at each site too (matching the repeated-cast form), not cached it in a local. This does not contradict the parent law: its DeleteItem/RegisterItemWobj/ShowMilestones evidence all started from source that ALREADY used repeated named-type casts (a developer-introduced regression the alias fixes); here the raw form had no shared variable to begin with, so a fresh inline cast is the FORM-PRESERVING conversion (identical reload count to the raw form) while a declared alias is the form-CHANGING one. Consequence: before introducing a declared alias for a multi-site field WRITE off a plain (non-walked/non-indexed) pointer, check whether the raw source already expresses every site as an independent dereference with no shared variable - if so, prefer a repeated inline cast (proven safe here up to 3-4 uses of one pointer, matching the parent law's own single-digit-site safety window) and A/B both forms regardless, exactly as the parent law already recommends doing per-function.
